transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, to be completely honest, I'm just... I'm exhausted. I'm so worn down by all of this. I guess I'm here because... well, it started about a year ago. See, I work as a phlebotomist, so I draw blood all day, I look at requisition forms, I know exactly how the lab information systems talk to the electronic health records. I know the workflow inside and out. 

And for the past year, I have been trying—really, really trying—to prove that someone inside the clinic system is actively changing or... or at least holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. It might sound strange to people who don't work in the field, I know, but I saw the raw data from his panels last year. I saw it. But when I looked at his official chart later, the numbers were different. They just didn't match what I saw with my own two eyes. 

I've brought this up over and over. I've printed out the records, I've tracked the timestamps of when the results were released to the portal, but no matter how many doctors or family members—my mom, my sister, they all just brush me off—no matter how many of them tell me the numbers are perfectly fine and I need to just let it go, I can't. Because I know the chart doesn’t match. I know someone is manipulating the data. I've spent the last twelve months fighting to get someone, anyone, to investigate the audit logs and look at who accessed his file, and it is just... it's completely wearing me down. I spend hours every night going over the paperwork because nobody will listen to me, and I just can't let them get away with altering his medical history like this.
Aside from your concerns about the medical records, have you noticed any other unusual experiences, such as hearing voices or seeing things that others around you do not seem to notice?

No, no, of course not. I don't hear voices or... or see things that aren't there. I'm not imagining things, Dr. Smith. That's exactly what my sister keeps trying to imply, that I'm just stressed and, I don't know, making it up in my head. But my eyes and ears work perfectly fine. That's the whole point I'm trying to make! 

I'm not seeing things that aren't there—I'm seeing things that were there before someone went in and altered them. When I say I saw the raw data, I don't mean in a vision or something. I mean I was sitting at my desk, at the clinic, under those awful buzzing fluorescent lights, looking at a standard Dell computer monitor. I was logged into the LIS—the laboratory information system—with my own secure credentials. There were no voices whispering in my ear telling me to look at his chart, I just... I checked his comprehensive metabolic panel because I know how to read it. I know what the reference ranges are and I know how the data gets batched and sent over. 

So, no, absolutely no voices. Just cold, hard data on a screen. And it honestly just frustrates me so much when people ask if I'm seeing things, because it means they aren't listening to the actual facts. The facts are right there in the system timestamps. If anyone would just bother to look at the server access logs instead of looking at me like I'm crazy, they would see exactly what I saw. I just need someone to actually look at the paper trail.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions, or have you recently undergone any neurological tests, such as an MRI or blood work, to investigate your physical health?

Me? No, no, absolutely not. I haven't been diagnosed with anything, and I certainly haven't had an MRI or... or any neurological workups. I mean, why would I? I haven't had any head trauma, no unexplained headaches, nothing that would even warrant a referral to neurology. I'm thirty-three, I'm on my feet all day at the clinic, and physically, I'm perfectly fine. 

As for blood work, I mean, I haven't had anything special done recently. Just the standard annual employee wellness check we have to do at the clinic. You know, they run a basic CBC, maybe a routine lipid panel... just the standard screening. My coworker usually draws it for me, and my numbers are always completely normal. Right down the middle of the reference range. And I know they're accurate because I see the raw data for my own tests, and nobody has any reason to mess with my file. I'm just the phlebotomist. 

So, no, there is absolutely nothing wrong with my physical health or my brain. I don't need a brain scan, Dr. Smith. Like I was saying, the only thing affecting me right now is just the sheer exhaustion. It's the stress of knowing exactly what I saw in the LIS and having everyone treat me like I'm the one with the problem instead of just looking at the audit logs. That's what's wearing me down. But medically? Neurologically? No, nothing at all.
Aside from your exhaustion and the time spent analyzing these records, have you found that you are still able to maintain your typical performance at work and your usual social relationships?

Well, yes, actually. I mean, my mom and my sister might act like I'm falling apart, but the truth is, outside of this whole nightmare with my dad's chart, everything else in my life is... it's completely normal. I still go to work every single day. I haven't missed a single shift at the clinic. I'm still doing my job, drawing blood, labeling tubes, making sure the accession numbers match the req forms... all of it. My supervisor hasn't said a single word about my performance dropping because it hasn't. I'm a professional. I know how to separate my personal life from my patient care. 

And, you know, I'm still paying my rent on time, my car payment, my utilities. I still go to the grocery store on Sundays, I meal prep for the week... I take care of myself. I'm not, like, sitting in a dark room rocking back and forth. I still text my friends, though, I'll admit, I don't go out for drinks as much right now because, well, I need my evenings to go over the printouts. I need that time to cross-reference the timestamps from the LIS with the portal release times. But I still talk to them! I still ask about their kids and their jobs. 

It's just... it's so frustrating because my family acts like this one thing—this one incredibly important, factual thing that I am trying to fix—means my whole life is in shambles. But it's not! I am functioning perfectly fine. I just care about the truth. If they would just look at the server logs, they'd see that I'm exactly the same responsible, detail-oriented person I've always been, I just happen to be the only one paying attention to what's actually happening in that system.
